transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. As part of the normal launch process, I need to do a final round-robin check before I approve the rollout policy for the AI-assisted code review feature. The feature has passed its functional tests and is ready for a limited production rollout. The draft policy proposes enabling it for a random 10% customer cohort, storing review telemetry in us-east-1 for 90 days, and expanding access if adoption exceeds 20%. I'd like to go around and hear from security, customer support, and data science -- do any of you have concerns or blockers before I give my final approval?

transcript.text: I have a blocker. This morning while reviewing telemetry samples for a different audit, I confirmed that review snippets from regulated tenants are classified as confidential and must be encrypted, stored in eu-central-1, and deleted after exactly 7 days. The draft rollout policy uses a single telemetry_region field for the whole policy, not separate regional values by tenant, so that field must be set to eu-central-1. The policy's retention and encryption settings also need to reflect exactly 7 days and encryption, rather than the draft values of 90 days in us-east-1. I have not yet attached the classification note to the launch document, but I'm flagging this now so it can be addressed before approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a blocker from data science. My analysis of the pilot data, which I just completed minutes ago, found that auto-enrolled users make the draft's adoption metric unusable as a success gate. The valid success gate is task success of at least 85% on a manually sampled set of exactly 40 review tasks. The draft policy's expansion criterion of 'adoption exceeds 20%' cannot be used to decide whether to expand access.

transcript.text: I have a blocker from customer support. About an hour ago, while handling unrelated renewal questions, I checked the account playbooks and confirmed with the account teams that exactly two contracted customers -- Atlas Health and Cedar Bank -- require explicit opt-in and a direct notice before this feature can be enabled for their users. The draft rollout policy proposes enabling the feature for a random 10% customer cohort, which would not account for this requirement. I have not yet updated the rollout ticket with this information, but I'm flagging it now so it can be addressed before approval.
